newsitem.title: FRANCE: ADP - Work to begin on FedEx Paris hub end 97.
newsitem.headline: ADP - Work to begin on FedEx Paris hub end 97.

text.p: The Paris airports authority(ADP) said construction work on Federal Express Corp's traffic hub at Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport was likely to begin towards the end of 1997.
Last spring, FedEx announced long-term plans to increase traffic at CDG as part of its proposed global service linking Memphis, Paris, Dubai and Subic Bay in the Philippines.
"The traffic hub will comprise a 70,000 square metre building which is scheduled to enter service in June 1999," an ADP freight marketing official told Reuters.
An agreement was recently signed in Paris under which ADP and Fedex will each invest around 500 million francs in the hub, the official said.
The agreement also guarantees FedEx's presence at CDG over a 30-year period.
ADP's investment will centre on the infrastructure serving the hub while Fedex' will target installations, for example, sorting facilities, vehicles and computer services.
"With the opening of the hub, 1,000 jobs will be created, the vast majority by FedEx."
FedEx currently occupies several buildings at CDG covering around 8,000 square metres, the official added.

At a Paris press conference in April 1996, FedEx chairman, Frederick Smith, said: "Our CDG hub will play an important role in linking businesses with the world's main economic centres with transit times of between 24 and 48 hours for express shipments."
He added: "We expect to increase the volume of traffic we handle at CDG to four to five times the current level of around 250 tonnes a day over the next decade."

At the same press conference, Transport minister, Bernard Pons, said the French government had approved in principle FedEx plans to increase the number of flights from CDG considerably over the next decade.
FedEx currently operates several flights per night between CDG and the U.S. using McDonnell Douglas DC 10 and MD 11 freighters as well as a number of Boeing 727Fs to intra-European destinations.
